record.paper_title: Properly Coloured Cycles and Paths: Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Lower bound for properly coloured paths in multigraphs
record.original_question: Let G be a c-edge-coloured multigraph of order n with minimum monochromatic degree d = δ_mon(G) ≥ 1. Must G always contain a properly coloured path of length at least min{n - 1, 2d}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.5. Let G be a c-edge-coloured multigraph of order n with δmon(G) = d ≥ 1. Then G has a PC path of length at least min{n − 1, 2d}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a multigraph on $n$ vertices whose edges are coloured with $c$ colours (a $c$-edge-coloured multigraph; multiple edges between the same pair of vertices are allowed, possibly with different colours). For a vertex $v\in V(G)$, the monochromatic degree of $v$ is
$$d^{\mathrm{mon}}(v)=\max_{i\in[c]} d_i(v),$$
where $d_i(v)$ is the number of edges of colour $i$ incident with $v$. Set $\delta_{\mathrm{mon}}(G)=\min_{v\in V(G)} d^{\mathrm{mon}}(v)$.

A path in $G$ is properly coloured (PC) if every two consecutive edges along the path have distinct colours.

Prove or disprove: every $c$-edge-coloured multigraph $G$ of order $n$ with $\delta_{\mathrm{mon}}(G)=d\ge 1$ contains a properly coloured path of length at least
$$\min\{n-1,\ 2d\}.$$

Related work on PC cycles and paths under monochromatic-degree conditions exists, but none of the located results clearly establishes or refutes the stated bound.

status_evidence.snippet: Recent work obtains bounds on the lengths of PC cycles under monochromatic-degree conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Related research on PC structures under monochromatic-degree conditions is active, but no source found that resolves the specific PC path bound min{n−1, 2d}.
